review.title: Justifiable homicide
review.plain: Lists the cases in which a homicide is justifiable, such as resisting an attempt to murder or to commit a felony, or defending habitation, property, or person.

review.title: Fear needed to justify homicide
review.plain: Says a bare fear of the offenses in subdivisions 2 and 3 of Section 197 is not enough; the circumstances must excite the fears of a reasonable person.

review.title: Presumed fear when force used at home
review.plain: Creates a presumption of reasonable fear when force likely to cause death or great bodily injury is used against an unlawful and forcible entrant into one's residence, and defines great bodily injury.

review.title: Acquittal when homicide justifiable
review.plain: Says that when a homicide appears justifiable or excusable, the person indicted must be fully acquitted and discharged at trial.

review.title: Mayhem defined
review.plain: Mayhem is unlawfully and maliciously depriving a person of a body member or disabling, disfiguring, or rendering it useless; this section states no penalty.
acts: deprives a human being of a member of his body, or disables, disfigures, or renders it useless, or cuts or disables the tongue, or puts out an eye, or slits the nose, ear, or lip

crimes.act: Deprives a human being of a member of his body, or disables, disfigures, or renders it useless, or cuts or disables the tongue, or puts out an eye, or slits the nose, ear, or lip
ways: Deprives a human being of a member of his body
Disables, disfigures, or renders it useless
Cuts or disables the tongue
Puts out an eye
Slits the nose, ear, or lip

penalties.penalty: No penalty is stated in this section

intent: Unlawfully and maliciously

review.title: Punishment for mayhem
review.plain: Mayhem is punishable by imprisonment in the state prison for two, four, or eight years.
acts: Mayhem

crimes.act: Commits mayhem

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for two, four, or eight years

review.title: Aggravated mayhem
review.plain: Aggravated mayhem is intentionally causing permanent disability or disfigurement, or depriving a person of a limb, organ, or member, with extreme indifference; it is punishable by life in state prison with the possibility of parole.
acts: intentionally causes permanent disability or disfigurement of another human being or deprives a human being of a limb, organ, or member of his or her body

crimes.act: Causes permanent disability or disfigurement of another human being or deprives a human being of a limb, organ, or member of his or her body
ways: Causes permanent disability or disfigurement of another human being
Deprives a human being of a limb, organ, or member of his or her body
conditions: Unlawfully, under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to the physical or psychological well-being of another person

penalties.penalty: Felony punishable by imprisonment in the state prison for life with the possibility of parole

intent: Intentionally
consequences: It is not necessary to prove an intent to kill

review.title: Torture
review.plain: Torture is inflicting great bodily injury on another with intent to cause cruel or extreme pain and suffering for revenge, extortion, persuasion, or a sadistic purpose; this section states no penalty.
acts: inflicts great bodily injury as defined in Section 12022.7 upon the person of another

crimes.act: Inflicts great bodily injury as defined in Section 12022.7 upon the person of another
conditions: The crime of torture does not require any proof that the victim suffered pain

penalties.penalty: No penalty is stated in this section

intent: With the intent to cause cruel or extreme pain and suffering for the purpose of revenge, extortion, persuasion, or for any sadistic purpose

review.title: Punishment for torture
review.plain: Torture is punishable by life in state prison, with parole eligibility only after at least seven years, or ten years in the stated case involving a child 14 or younger.
acts: torture

crimes.act: Commits torture

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for a term of life

consequences: A defendant imprisoned for torture shall not be eligible for parole until they have served at least seven years, pursuant to Section 3046

For a crime of torture committed on or after January 1, 2026, if the defendant is an adult who had care or custody of the victim and the victim was 14 years of age or younger at the time of the crime, the defendant shall not be eligible for parole until they have served at least 10 years

review.title: Kidnapping
review.plain: Kidnapping is forcibly or by fear taking or holding a person and carrying them elsewhere, enticing a child under 14, or bringing a person into the state; this section states no penalty.

hires, persuades, entices, decoys, or seduces by false promises, misrepresentations, or the like, any child under the age of 14 years to go out of this country, state, or county, or into another part of the same county
takes or holds, detains, or arrests any person, with a design to take the person out of this state
abducts or takes by force or fraud any person contrary to the law of the place where that act is committed, and brings, sends, or conveys that person within the limits of this state

terms: "Force" for kidnapping an unresisting infant or child: the amount of physical force required to take and carry the child away a substantial distance for an illegal purpose or with an illegal intent

crimes.act: Steals or takes, or holds, detains, or arrests any person in this state, and carries the person into another country, state, or county, or into another part of the same county
ways: Steals or takes
Holds, detains, or arrests
conditions: Done forcibly, or by any other means of instilling fear
The person is carried into another country, state, or county, or into another part of the same county
exceptions: Subdivisions (a) to (d) do not apply to any person who steals, takes, entices away, detains, conceals, or harbors any child under the age of 14 years, if that act is taken to protect the child from danger of imminent harm

penalties.penalty: No penalty is stated in this section

crimes.act: Hires, persuades, entices, decoys, or seduces by false promises, misrepresentations, or the like, any child under the age of 14 years to go out of this country, state, or county, or into another part of the same county

Persuades

penalties.penalty: No penalty is stated in this section

penalties.penalty: No penalty is stated in this section

intent: For the purpose and with the intent to sell that person into slavery or involuntary servitude, or otherwise to employ that person for his or her own use, or to the use of another, without the free will and consent of that persuaded person

crimes.act: Abducts or takes by force or fraud any person contrary to the law of the place where that act is committed, and brings, sends, or conveys that person within the limits of this state
ways: Abducts
Takes by force or fraud

The person is afterwards found within the limits of this state

Subdivisions (a) to (d) do not apply to any person acting under Section 834 or 837

penalties.penalty: No penalty is stated in this section

review.title: Punishment for kidnapping
review.plain: Kidnapping is punishable by three, five, or eight years in state prison, or five, eight, or eleven years if the victim is under 14; probation requires 12 months in county jail except in unusual cases.
acts: Kidnapping

crimes.act: Commits kidnapping
exceptions: The under-14 tier is not applicable to the taking, detaining, or concealing, of a minor child by a biological parent, a natural father, as specified in Section 7611 of the Family Code, an adoptive parent, or a person who has been granted access to the minor child by a court order

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for three, five, or eight years

penalties.if: the person kidnapped is under 14 years of age at the time of the commission of the crime
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for 5, 8, or 11 years

consequences: In all cases in which probation is granted, the court shall, except in unusual cases where the interests of justice would best be served by a lesser penalty, require as a condition of the probation that the person be confined in the county jail for 12 months
If the court grants probation without requiring the defendant to be confined in the county jail for 12 months, it shall specify its reason or reasons for imposing a lesser penalty

review.title: Kidnapping for ransom or to commit a crime
review.plain: Kidnapping for ransom, reward, or extortion is a felony punishable by life, without parole if the victim dies or is harmed; kidnapping to commit robbery or a sex offense is life with parole.
acts: seizes, confines, inveigles, entices, decoys, abducts, conceals, kidnaps, or carries away another person by any means whatsoever with intent to hold or detain, or who holds or detains, that person for ransom, reward, or to commit extortion or to exact from another person any money or valuable thing, or a person who aids or abets any such act
kidnaps or carries away an individual to commit robbery, rape, oral copulation, sodomy, or any violation of Section 264.1, 288, 289, or former Section 262

crimes.act: Seizes, confines, inveigles, entices, decoys, abducts, conceals, kidnaps, or carries away another person by any means whatsoever with intent to hold or detain, or holds or detains, that person for ransom, reward, or to commit extortion or to exact from another person any money or valuable thing, or aids or abets any such act
ways: Seizes, confines, inveigles, entices, decoys, abducts, conceals, kidnaps, or carries away another person
Holds or detains that person
Aids or abets any such act
conditions: For ransom, reward, or to commit extortion or to exact from another person any money or valuable thing

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a felony

penalties.if: a person subjected to that act suffers death or bodily harm, or is intentionally confined in a manner that exposes that person to a substantial likelihood of death
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for life without possibility of parole

penalties.if: no person subjected to that act suffers death or bodily harm
penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for life with the possibility of parole

consequences: When probation is granted, the court shall, except in unusual cases where the interests of justice would best be served by a lesser penalty, require as a condition of the probation that the person be confined in the county jail for 12 months
If the court grants probation without requiring the defendant to be confined in the county jail for 12 months, it shall specify its reason or reasons for imposing a lesser penalty

crimes.act: Kidnaps or carries away an individual to commit robbery, rape, oral copulation, sodomy, or any violation of Section 264.1, 288, 289, or former Section 262
conditions: The movement of the victim is beyond that merely incidental to the commission of, and increases the risk of harm to the victim over and above that necessarily present in, the intended underlying offense

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for life with the possibility of parole

consequences: Subdivision (b) does not supersede or affect Section 667.61

A person may not be punished under subdivision (b) and Section 667.61 for the same act that constitutes a violation of both

When probation is granted, the court shall, except in unusual cases where the interests of justice would best be served by a lesser penalty, require as a condition of the probation that the person be confined in the county jail for 12 months
If the court grants probation without requiring the defendant to be confined in the county jail for 12 months, it shall specify its reason or reasons for imposing a lesser penalty

review.title: Kidnapping during a carjacking
review.plain: Kidnapping another person during a carjacking to facilitate it is punishable by life in state prison with the possibility of parole.
acts: kidnaps another person who is not a principal in the commission of the carjacking

crimes.act: Kidnaps another person who is not a principal in the commission of the carjacking

The victim is moved a substantial distance from the vicinity of the carjacking
The movement of the victim increases the risk of harm to the victim over and above that necessarily present in the crime of carjacking itself

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for life with the possibility of parole

consequences: In all cases in which probation is granted, the court shall, except in unusual cases where the interests of justice would best be served by a lesser penalty, require as a condition of the probation that the person be confined in the county jail for 12 months
If the court grants probation without requiring the defendant to be confined in the county jail for 12 months, it shall specify its reason or reasons for imposing a lesser penalty

review.title: Posing as kidnapper for ransom
review.plain: Posing as a kidnapper, or as someone able to obtain a victim's release, to obtain ransom, reward, or money is a felony punishable by imprisonment for two, three, or four years.
acts: poses as, or in any manner represents himself to be a person who has seized, confined, inveigled, enticed, decoyed, abducted, concealed, kidnapped or carried away any person

crimes.act: Poses as, or in any manner represents himself to be, a person who has seized, confined, inveigled, enticed, decoyed, abducted, concealed, kidnapped or carried away any person, or who holds or detains such person, or who has aided or abetted any such act, or who has the influence, power, or ability to obtain the release of such person
ways: Poses as a person who has seized, confined, inveigled, enticed, decoyed, abducted, concealed, kidnapped or carried away any person
Poses as a person who holds or detains such person
Poses as a person who has aided or abetted any such act
Poses as a person who has the influence, power, or ability to obtain the release of such person
exceptions: Nothing in this section prohibits any person who, in good faith believes that he can rescue any person who has been seized, confined, inveigled, enticed, decoyed, abducted, concealed, kidnapped or carried away, and who has had no part in, or connection with, such confinement, inveigling, decoying, abducting, concealing, kidnapping, or carrying away, from offering to rescue or obtain the release of such person for a monetary consideration or other thing of value

penalties.penalty: Felony punishable by imprisonment for two, three or four years

intent: For the purpose of obtaining any ransom or reward, or to extort or exact from any person any money or thing of value

review.title: False imprisonment as shield or to avoid arrest
review.plain: False imprisonment of a person to protect against arrest, substantially increasing risk of harm, or to use as a shield, is punishable under subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for three, five, or eight years.

crimes.act: Commits the offense of false imprisonment, as defined in Section 236, against a person
conditions: For purposes of protection from arrest, which substantially increases the risk of harm to the victim, or for purposes of using the person as a shield

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 for three, five, or eight years

review.title: Robbery
review.plain: Robbery is the felonious taking of personal property from another's person or immediate presence, against their will, by force or fear; this section states no penalty.

crimes.act: Takes personal property in the possession of another, from his person or immediate presence, and against his will
conditions: Accomplished by means of force or fear

penalties.penalty: No penalty is stated in this section

intent: Feloniously

review.plain: Says the fear mentioned in Section 211 may be fear of unlawful injury to the person robbed or relatives, or of immediate unlawful injury to anyone in the person robbed's company.

review.title: Degrees of robbery
review.plain: Sets which robberies are of the first degree, such as those of transit operators and passengers, in inhabited dwellings, or at automated teller machines, and says all others are second degree.

review.title: Punishment for robbery
review.plain: Robbery of the first degree carries three to nine years in state prison depending on the case, and second degree carries two, three, or five years.
acts: Robbery of the first degree
Robbery of the second degree
attempted robbery in violation of paragraph (2) of subdivision (a)

crimes.act: Commits robbery of the first degree

penalties.penalty: In all cases other than that specified in subparagraph (A), by imprisonment in the state prison for three, four, or six years

review.title: Train robbery and train interference
review.plain: Boarding a train to rob passengers, or interfering with railroad track, signals, or trains with intent to rob, is a felony; this section states no term.
acts: goes upon or boards any railroad train, car or engine
interferes in any manner with any switch, rail, sleeper, viaduct, culvert, embankment, structure or appliance pertaining to or connected with any railroad
places any dynamite or other explosive substance or material upon or near the track of any railroad
sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle
stops any such train, car or engine, or slackens the speed thereof

crimes.act: Goes upon or boards any railroad train, car or engine; interferes in any manner with any switch, rail, sleeper, viaduct, culvert, embankment, structure or appliance pertaining to or connected with any railroad; places any dynamite or other explosive substance or material upon or near the track of any railroad; sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle; shows, masks, extinguishes or alters any light or other signal; exhibits or compels any other person to exhibit any false light or signal; stops any such train, car or engine, or slackens the speed thereof; or compels or attempts to compel any person in charge or control thereof to stop any such train, car or engine, or slacken the speed thereof
ways: Goes upon or boards any railroad train, car or engine

Compels or attempts to compel any person in charge or control thereof to stop any such train, car or engine, or slacken the speed thereof

penalties.penalty: Guilty of a felony

intent: With the intention of robbing any passenger or other person on such train, car or engine, of any personal property thereon in the possession or charge or under the control of any such passenger or other person

review.title: Carjacking
review.plain: Carjacking is the felonious taking of a motor vehicle from another's person or immediate presence by force or fear; it is punishable by three, five, or nine years in state prison.
acts: taking of a motor vehicle in the possession of another, from his or her person or immediate presence, or from the person or immediate presence of a passenger of the motor vehicle, against his or her will

crimes.act: Takes a motor vehicle in the possession of another, from his or her person or immediate presence, or from the person or immediate presence of a passenger of the motor vehicle, against his or her will
conditions: Accomplished by means of force or fear

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the state prison for a term of three, five, or nine years

intent: Feloniously
With the intent to either permanently or temporarily deprive the person in possession of the motor vehicle of his or her possession
consequences: This section shall not be construed to supersede or affect Section 211
A person may be charged with a violation of this section and Section 211
No defendant may be punished under this section and Section 211 for the same act which constitutes a violation of both

review.title: Assault on public officials
review.plain: Assaulting listed officials such as judges, prosecutors, or peace officers in retaliation for or to prevent official duties is a wobbler; attempted murder of them carries 15 years to life.
acts: commits any assault upon the President or Vice President of the United States
attempts to commit murder against any person listed in subdivision (a)

crimes.act: Commits any assault upon the President or Vice President of the United States, the Governor of any state or territory, any justice, judge, or former judge of any local, state, or federal court of record, any commissioner, referee, or other subordinate judicial officer of any court of record, the secretary or director of any executive agency or department of the United States or any state or territory, or any other official of the United States or any state or territory holding elective office, any mayor, city council member, county supervisor, sheriff, district attorney, prosecutor or assistant prosecutor of any local, state, or federal prosecutor’s office, a former prosecutor or assistant prosecutor, public defender or assistant public defender, a former public defender or assistant public defender, the chief of police of any municipal police department, any peace officer, any juror in any local, state, or federal court of record, or the immediate family of any of these officials

penalties.penalty: Imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year or imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170

crimes.act: Attempts to commit murder against any person listed in subdivision (a)

penalties.penalty: Confined in the state prison for a term of 15 years to life

intent: In retaliation for or to prevent the performance of the victim’s official duties
consequences: The provisions of Article 2.5 (commencing with Section 2930) of Chapter 7 of Title 1 of Part 3 shall apply to reduce any minimum term of 15 years in a state prison imposed pursuant to this section, but that person shall not otherwise be released on parole prior to that time

review.title: Derailing a train
review.plain: Unlawfully obstructing or setting fire to railroad track or bridges with intent to derail or wreck a train is a felony punishable by life in state prison without possibility of parole.

places any dynamite or other explosive material or any other obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad
sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle

ways: Throws out a switch, removes a rail, or places any obstruction on any railroad
Places any dynamite or other explosive material or any other obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad
Sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle

penalties.penalty: Felony punishable by imprisonment in the state prison for life without possibility of parole

With the intention of derailing, blowing up, or wrecking any such train, car or engine

review.title: Obstructing railroad track with gross negligence
review.plain: Unlawfully and with gross negligence placing an obstruction on a railroad track that damages or derails a train or injures a passenger or employee is punishable in county jail, under Section 1170(h), or by fine.

crimes.act: Places or causes to be placed any obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad

intent: Unlawfully

review.title: Wrecking a train
review.plain: Unlawfully obstructing, blowing up, or burning railroad track or bridges with intent to wreck a train and doing so is a felony; death or life without parole if someone dies, otherwise life with parole.
acts: throws out a switch, removes a rail, or places any obstruction on any railroad
places any dynamite or other explosive material or any other obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad
sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle

crimes.act: Throws out a switch, removes a rail, or places any obstruction on any railroad; places any dynamite or other explosive material or any other obstruction upon or near the track of any railroad; or sets fire to any railroad bridge or trestle over which any such train, car or engine must pass
ways: Throws out a switch, removes a rail, or places any obstruction on any railroad

review.title: Wrecking a common carrier vehicle

review.title: Throwing objects at trains, buses, or vessels
